title: Audit evidence synthesis & short-answer CISO brief
body:
Purpose and audience:
This is a two-page CISO-facing brief plus a short-answer bank for customer security questionnaires. It synthesizes the most readily verifiable evidence we can point to for RBAC v2, audit-log schema, SIEM export mappings, and the evidence automation paths we have in-flight. Primary audience: CISO/InfoSec reviewers and security architects who need concise answers with direct evidence references.

Status/notes to reviewers:
- Draft: aimed to replace long-form audit playbooks in first customer responses.
- Goal: provide 1–2 sentence short answers + 1–2 supporting artifacts (link or path) per common questionnaire item.
- Open questions: retention policy nuance for backups (see Q:1), PII redaction specifics for customer-managed private deployments.

Executive summary (1 paragraph):
Redwood Inference operates RBAC v2 across control plane and data plane with explicit role inheritance and immutable audit events for role changes. Audit logs are emitted in JSON with a canonical schema (timestamp, actor_id, actor_type, action, resource_type, resource_id, before, after, request_id, region, tenant_id) and are exported to customer SIEMs via compressed daily bundles plus near-real-time streaming webhook for high-priority events. We maintain an evidence automation layer (ETL jobs + evidence index) that maps questionnaire topics to concrete artifacts (logs, policy definitions, config snapshots, Confluence proof) to reduce manual pull requests during assessments.

Short-answer bank (concise answers + evidence pointers):
Q: How do you enforce least privilege?
A: RBAC v2 enforces least privilege through role templates and scoped roles; all policy changes require an audited role-change workflow and optional approval. Evidence: (1) RBAC policy JSON snapshot - confluence:SECURITY-EVIDENCE-HUB-87/rbac-v2-policy-2026-01, (2) audit event for role assignment example - logs/export/role-change-example-2026-01-14.json (Jira SEC-4132).

Q: Where are audit logs stored and how long are they retained?
A: Primary storage is hardened object storage with server-side encryption; default retention 365 days for hosted customers; Dedicated/Private can configure retention via retention_policy field in tenancy config. Evidence: (1) retention policy doc - confluence:retention-policies, (2) sample SIEM export manifest - s3://redwood-logs/exports/manifest-2026-02-01.json.

Q: Can we get a schema for audit logs?
A: Yes — canonical audit schema is available and stable across releases; see file 'audit-log-canonical-schema-v1.json' with field definitions and examples. Evidence: (1) schema file - github:repo/redwood-infra/blob/main/observability/audit-schema.json, (2) sample event - logs/examples/authz-check-2026-01-30.json.

Q: How are role changes protected from tampering?
A: Role-change events are recorded immutably in the audit stream with cryptographic signing of the export bundle and checksum verification on ingest; change approvals are stored in the control plane with MFA enforced for approvers. Evidence: (1) control-plane approvals audit - logs/export/approvals-2026-01.json, (2) checksum + signature manifest - hashes/exports/2026-01-signature.txt.

Q: How do you prevent sensitive data leakage in logs?
A: We apply structured log redaction rules at the emission layer; PII fields are identified by schema tags and replaced or tokenized before export. Evidence: (1) redaction rules doc - confluence:PII-redaction-rulebook, (2) sample sanitized event - logs/examples/sanitized-2026-01.json.

Q: How do you deliver logs to our SIEM?
A: Two modes: (A) batch exports — encrypted daily bundles to customer S3/secure FTP, and (B) near-real-time streaming via customer-configured webhook or syslog endpoint. Evidence: (1) SIEM integration spec - confluence:siem-integration-spec-v2, (2) example webhook event - logs/webhook/sample-login-fail-2026-02-05.json.

Mapping appendix (high-value fields to proofs) - abbreviated:
- actor_id, actor_type -> identity proof: auth service token logs, idp-link (confluence:identity-integration).
- action -> access-control policy snapshot (rbac export), sample event with before/after.
- request_id -> distributed trace link (console link + tracing span id in event).
- tenant_id -> tenancy config + enrollment manifest.
- before/after -> config snapshots accessible in evidence index.
Evidence locations: logs/export/, policy-snapshots/, confluence:..., github:... (see linked_artifacts).

Evidence automation overview (how to reduce manual pulls):
- Evidence index: small service that maps questionnaire keys to artifact queries (ELK query, S3 prefix, Confluence page).
- Connector runners: small ETL jobs that can produce a customer-facing artifact bundle (PDF + manifest) on demand.
- Runbook for assessors: steps to run automated bundle for a customer (1. open SEC Jira ticket, 2. run connector with tenant_id, 3. upload bundle to secure share).
- In-progress work: automated snapshotter for RBAC v2 policies (PR: github:repo/redwood-infra#PR-2287) to produce time-stamped JSON and human-readable FAQ.

SIEM export field mapping (practical notes for auditors):
- Timestamps are ISO8601 UTC. Ensure SIEM ingest preserves timezone.
- Event type normalization: our export includes canonical "event_type" and vendor-specific tags. Use event_type for rule authorship.
- Role-change events have delta fields under 'before' and 'after' — auditors should look for 'effect' and 'grantee' keys.

One-pager (copyable):
Title: Redwood Inference — Audit & RBAC Snapshot- Summary (1 line): Canonical RBAC v2 with immutable audit events and configurable SIEM export (batch + near-real-time).- What we ship as evidence: policy snapshots, signed audit exports, sample events, retention manifest, redaction policy.- How we automate: evidence index + connector runners produce customer bundles on-demand.- How to validate: provide tenant_id and time range; we will deliver signed export bundle and a manifest mapping artifacts to questionnaire claims.

Operational caveats and talking points (for sales/solutions):
- Dedicated/private customers can elect to keep audit logs in their own cloud tenancy; in those cases we provide export tooling rather than ingest.
- For high-sensitivity customers we recommend 2x export (real-time webhook to customer SIEM + daily signed bundle) for defense-in-depth.
- When asked about SOC2/ISO artifacts, point to standard evidence index entries and the auditor onboarding checklist (confluence:auditor-onboarding-v2).

Unresolved / follow-ups (TODOs):
- Q: Clarify retention exceptions for backups and cold storage (ask infra/legal).
- Q: Finalize the sample event set for RBAC role-delegation edge cases (owner: Devin).
- Add quick script snippets for connector runner invocation to evidence runbook.

Appendix: quick runbook for producing a customer bundle (operator facing)
1) Create SEC-<customer>-evidence ticket and include tenant_id + time window.
2) Run evidence-indexer with tenant_id: python tools/indexer.py --tenant <id> --range 2026-01-01:2026-01-31
3) Artifacts produced: signed-audit-bundle.tar.gz, policy-snapshots.zip, manifest.json, human-readable FAQ.pdf
4) Upload to secure share and link in ticket; optionally push to customer S3 if requested.

Notes to self: keep this doc lean; separate long-form playbook into 'audit-evidence-playbook-longform' and wire automation run examples in a second file.

Change log (short):

End of brief.
